title: Colposcopy
what: A gynecologist looks at your cervix through a special magnifying device. The device does not go inside your body.
why: If your smear test shows changes, if you have HPV, or if the doctor saw an area that needs a closer look.
tell_doctor: The date your last period started
If you are pregnant or might be pregnant
If you are allergic to iodine

prepare.title: Day of your cycle
prepare.text: Not during your period. It is usually best in the first days after it ends. Check with your doctor.

prepare.title: 1 to 2 days before
prepare.text: No sex, douching, tampons, vaginal suppositories, or creams.

bring: Results of your last smear test and HPV test
steps: You sit in the gynecology chair
The doctor puts in a speculum, like in a regular exam
The device with a lens and a light stays outside, next to the chair
The cervix is coated with a weak vinegar solution, then an iodine solution
If needed, a tiny piece of tissue is taken for testing
feel: The speculum feels like pressure, like in a regular exam
The solutions may sting a little
If a tissue sample is taken: a quick pinch or a cramp
after: For a few days you may have dark discharge. This is from the solutions
After a tissue sample: light spotting for a few days
If a sample was taken, usually no sex, tampons, or baths for a few days. Your doctor will say how long
Tissue results usually come in 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Heavy bleeding, more than a normal period
A high fever, strong pain in the lower belly, or bad-smelling discharge

faq.a: Usually not. It feels like a regular gynecology exam. If a tissue sample is taken, you feel a quick, unpleasant pinch.

faq.q: Can I have a colposcopy while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes, it is safe. Tell your doctor you are pregnant. A tissue sample is usually taken only for a serious reason.

reminders.text: Colposcopy in 2 days. From today: no sex, douching, tampons, or vaginal suppositories.
